the aortic valve of humans and common animal species (i.e., ovine and porine) differ mechanically and histologically.

the biomechanical characterization of human, ovine, and porcine aortic valves.

the ovine model appears to be the most appropriate model for studying the aortic valve disease in humans.

the ovine model is the best available animal model for the aged human aortic valve.

the biomechanical and histological properties of the human, porcine and ovine aortic valves are different, and these differences are significant enough to question the suitability of the commonly used animal models for the study of human aortic valves.

a thorough understanding of animal models, and their differences with respect to humans, is necessary for the establishment of appropriate animal models and for the evaluation of new valve treatment techniques.
